comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
https://i.redd.it/an5jaiiq7txh1.png



Here is a slop. Let's just start with this as a baseline, so at least there's a shared universe we can draw one agreed-upon data point from: this is an image from GPT imagegen, nothing was done to try and make it look nice, it is pure slop. 

It's not the worst slop I ever had imagegen made. It's still slop. Unacceptable to me as meaningful artwork. 

  
For me, 'slop' kind of has a narrow and specific meaning - it is art that has to be subtractively sculpted into something that would be acceptable to my tastes. You can't really add to or 'refine' this image - it is already fully detailed and colored, it's just that the fine detail work is incredibly bad. So you have to find ways to rip that out. 

Maybe you pixelize this, stripping out the slop in one go by getting a bit of a mess in return that you then go in and additively fix on more manageable scale. Maybe you go in by hand and painstakingly fix every single greeble and nonsensical branch or leaf. 

The critical thing is that the work you have to do on slop is all subtractive. You cut things out, you flatten wrong details, you simplify overly complex or just plain bad texturing. 

  
This is the critical difference between the coding and the artwork. The coding is additive; you just build with it. The art has to be cleaned-up - the fun parts, the parts involving the most expression and motion and play - are already done. You're just chiselling away at garbage, hoping to find a prize underneath. 

  
So, it's not that the AI slop looks bad and must be fixed. Like you say, that is every piece of art ever.

It is that the AI art is already made, the fun part is over, and now you're just the art janitor and garbage truck man.   
  
  
So, some of us are hoping that we eventually do get additive image gen at some point, but it's not clear if that's even possible. Stable Diffusion - the process all generated art is made with - works in a very specific way, and it might not ever be able to create nice clean images that can be built up on top of rather than cut away at.

comments.author: RoundTableTTRPG
comments.body: you are wrong, slop is a very specific fail state that humans are not generally capable of. A human dev writes 200 lines of code to execute the core engine of their game and it fails because he for got like 5 commas and several integers are strings. AI slop is 5000 lines of immaculate code that runs, but none of the variables are connected, a buch of randomly siloed sections of the core engine are easier to modify whole cloth than to plug variables into, etc. You tell it to change a string to an integer so you can use it as a variable and it does that, a single line edit, and now the code base is 5230 lines.

comments.author: Arkenhammer
comments.body:
Early work isn’t slop as long as you recognize that it is early work and don’t put it on Steam. Slop is a product built with obvious disregard for the consumer. It is a game that lacks empathy for the player.

Take Sony’s Concorde. It was slop not because it was unrefined but because it was refined toward the wrong goals. It was built because Sony wanted a live service game that could continuously milk players for money. They spent lots of time optimizing their micro transactions and not enough on making a game people actually wanted to play. $400M burned and still slop.
